pattern.description: The Salesforce call side panel left over from the previous screen slides out to the left while the Agent Builder page slides left with it to take the full frame width. Energy is flat and then drops off sharply, which reads as a short ease-out push. The cursor then hovers the Agentforce SDR card, which snaps to its highlighted state.
pattern.why_premium: A single horizontal push carries the viewer from the live call to the builder without a cut, so the narration's 'these are just a few of the standard agents' lands on a clean full-width catalog, and the hover state points straight at the first agent.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.timeline().to('.call-panel', {xPercent: -100, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out'}).fromTo('.builder', {x: 300}, {x: 0, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out'}, '<').set('.sdr-card', {className: '+=is-hover'}, '+=0.4'); the hover is an instant state change, not a tween.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 200, mass: 1}}); panel translateX = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [0, -280]); builder translateX = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [300, 0]); toggle the card's hover border with a hard frame check (frame >= hoverFrame).

notes: camera.move is none, so the leftward shift is reported as content motion. The cursor moves with the builder layer (screen recording), so it is not listed as a separate element. Whether the exiting panel is pushed or covered by the builder is hard to tell from the filmstrip. The card's title shortening may be a UI detail of the recording rather than an authored animation.
